fullData.title: Adding Decimals on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Leo walks $0.4$ miles to the park, and then walks another $0.3$ miles to the library. Use the number line to find the total distance Leo walks.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Start at the first distance on the number line and count forward by tenths to find the total distance.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, showing a jump of 0.4 from 0 to the park.

annotations.steps: I draw a jump starting at zero and moving forward by four tenth-divisions to reach zero point four.
annotations.strategy: I notice that starting at zero helps me track the exact distance Leo walked first.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects whole number counting on a number line to decimal numbers by using tenths as equal parts of one whole.
annotations.narrative: On the number line, locate Start at $0$ and follow the $0.4\text{ miles}$ to the point labeled Park at $0.4$.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 with 10 divisions, showing a start at 0.4 and three jumps of 0.1 forward, landing at 0.7.

annotations.steps: Start at 0.4 on the number line and make three jumps of 0.1 to the right, landing on 0.7.
annotations.strategy: I notice that adding decimals on a number line works just like whole numbers, so I count forward by tenths.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition to the standard measurement and counting models used for whole numbers.
annotations.narrative: From Park at $0.4$, count forward $3$ tenths ($0.3$) to reach the point labeled Library at $0.7$. This means Leo walks a total distance of $0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7\text{ miles}$.

challenge.prompt: Starting at the park at $0.4$, how many jumps of $0.1$ forward should Leo make to add $0.3$ miles?
challenge.rationale: Since each jump represents $0.1$ miles, adding $0.3$ miles takes $3$ jumps; counting the starting mark at $0.4$ as a move would incorrectly give $4$.

specs.title: Plot the walk to park
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Understand how to represent an initial decimal distance by marking a jump from zero on a number line partitioned into tenths.
specs.seedNotes: Draw a number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, highlighting the interval from 0 (Start) to 0.4 (Park).

specs.title: Count forward to library
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize decimal addition as continuing forward along the number line by jumping additional tenths to reach the total sum.
specs.seedNotes: From 0.4, show 3 jumps of 0.1 forward to land at 0.7 labeled Library, arriving at 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7 miles.
